newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-NOVOTNA CRUSHES SANCHEZ VICARIO TO REACH SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA CRUSHES SANCHEZ VICARIO TO REACH SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Jana Novotna extended her impressive victory streak Friday and snapped a personal slide against doubles partner Arantxa Sanchez Vicario with a one-sided win in the quarter-finals of the Chase Championships.

Novotna, beaten the last seven times she had faced Sanchez, crushed the third seed 6-0 6-3 to reach the semifinals of the $2 million season-ending tournament and give herself a chance at winning a fourth straight tournament.
"It's a long time since I beat her," said Novotna, who had gone five years since she last defeated Sanchez, at Leipzig. "I couldn't have picked a better time to do it."
Novotna dominated the usually steady Spaniard from the start, blunting Sanchez's passing shots with some dazzling net play.
When she was not placing volley winners and smashing overhead putaways, Novotna was driving the ball deep into the corners to dictate the other points.

The points came with such swiftness that 13 minutes into the match the fifth seed from the Czech Republic led 5-0. The sixth game was the first in which Sanchez managed to reach deuce -- and that was after squandering a 0-40 lead to the rampaging Novotna.

"I think normally when you lose a match you are disappointed," said Sanchez. "But today, Jana played better than me and that's the way the match went. Everything worked out well for her and nothing went right for me."

Novotna, who has won three Grand Slam doubles titles with Sanchez as her partner, had won six of her first seven matches against the Spaniard, who at 25 is three years her junior. Their career series now stands at 8-7 in Sanchez's favour.
The brilliant recent run by Novotna, whose singles record this season is a mighty 54-12, has lifted her to her highest spot ever in the rankings -- number three.
Next up for Novotna is world number one Steffi Graf, who retired during their singles final in Philadelphia last week because of back spasms after losing the first set to the Czech.
"I've still got a long way to go and there is Steffi in the way," said Novotna, eyeing a fourth consecutive tournament title despite trailing Graf 25-4 in their career series.
"But if I keep playing like I am, there is a good chance."
